text:
Christian Dvorak had his moment last Saturday: he opened the scoring against Montreal, the team that traded him to Philadelphia, and the Canadiens answered 16 seconds later. It was part of a four-game point streak that ended Tuesday, and his 16 points in 27 games is about the pace you'd expect from him.

The scoring is fine. The five-on-five picture isn't. Philadelphia gets just 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his team has scored 3.2 more goals than those chances deserved while he's out there. That's how a line gets outplayed and still breaks even for a while.

Some of it is the job. Evolving-Hockey had him facing top-3% competition last season, and only 38% of his even-strength time is spent in the offensive zone. But NHL EDGE puts his hardest shot near the bottom of the league, and his own shot quality is down from last season. He's a useful, honest middle-six center being asked to do more than that.
